result.topic_en: Euler concludes that sums of three cube roots with equal cubic residues are divisible by a prime 3n+1, gives the example of divisor 19, and states and begins proving the theorem that numbers pp+3qq have prime divisors of form 3n+1 but never of form 3n−1.
result.transcription:
122 RESIDVA EX DIVIS. POTESTATVM
$f+g+h$; $fg+fh+gh$; $ff+gg+hh$
ſingulae diuiſionem per $3n+1$ admittent.
Coroll.
75. Ita pro diuiſore 19 videmus hos tres cubos $4^3$, $6^3$ et $9^3$ idem reſiduum 7 dare; vnde ob $f=4$, $g=6$, $h=9$ fit $f+g+h=19$; $fg+fh+gh=114=6.19$ et $ff+gg+hh=133=7.19$.
Theorema.
76. Semper numeri huius formae $pp+3qq$ exhiberi poſſunt per numerum primum huius formae $3n+1$ diuiſibiles. At vero nulla eiusmodi datur formula $pp+3qq$, quae per vllum numerum primum huius formae $3n-1$ ſit diuiſibilis.
Demonſtratio.
Si $3n+1$ eſt numerus primus, tum tres adeo cubi $f^3$, $g^3$, $h^3$ quorum radices ipſo ſunt minores, exhiberi poſſunt, qui per $3n+1$ diuiſi idem reſiduum relinquant; vnde $g^3-f^3$ per $3n+1$ diuiſionem admittet hincque etiam $ff+fg+gg$. At haec forma eſt vel $(f+\frac{1}{2}g)^2+3(\frac{1}{2}g)^2$ ſi $g$ ſit numerus par, vel $(\frac{1}{2}f+g)^2+3(\frac{1}{2}f)^2$ ſi $f$ ſit par, vel $(\frac{f-g}{2})^2+3(\frac{f+g}{2})^2$, ſi ambo ſint impares, vnde forma $ff+fg+gg$ ſemper ad hanc $pp+3qq$ reducitur.
At ſi $3n-1$ ſit diuiſor primus, omnes cubi, quorum radices ipſo ſunt minores, diuerſa praebent

items.quote: Semper numeri huius formae $pp+3qq$ exhiberi poſſunt per numerum primum huius formae $3n+1$ diuiſibiles. At vero nulla eiusmodi datur formula $pp+3qq$, quae per vllum numerum primum huius formae $3n-1$ ſit diuiſibilis.
items.english: Numbers of the form pp+3qq can always be found that are divisible by a prime of the form 3n+1. But there is no formula pp+3qq of this kind that is divisible by any prime of the form 3n−1.
f+g+h, fg+fh+gh and ff+gg+hh will each be divisible by 3n+1.
